And no one is more closely linked to the genocide that took place in the small town in eastern Bosnia than Ratko Mladic , the former commander-in-chief of the Bosnian Serb army. Although the United Nations had declared Srebrenica a "safe area," Bosnian Serb forces attacked the town. Within just a few days in July 1995, they expelled women and children, then killed more than 8,300 unarmed Muslim boys and men in the nearby village of Potocari — on Mladic's direct orders, according to the verdict handed down by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) in The Hague 22 years later. At the time, Srebrenica was the largest massacre in Europe since World War II . The ICTY classified it as genocide. stories.title: Can new Apple CEO John Ternus fix the tech giant's AI woes?
stories.summary: John Ternus is just the third Apple CEO in 30 years. His primary challenge is to correct the company's faltering AI strategy to preserve its position as a big tech leader.

stories.title: 200 bikers gather at Italy's Castel Gandolfo for motorcycle blessing
stories.summary: Around 200 bikers gathered at Lake Castel Gandolfo for a motorcycle blessing, with Father Tadeusz Rozmus calling for brotherhood, respect and safer roads.

stories.title: Buenos Aires welcomes 800 couples for Tango BA World Championship
stories.summary: Tango BA brings 800 couples from 47 countries to Buenos Aires, with world championship finals taking place at the Teatro Gran Rex.

stories.title: South African airline Airlink defends dramatic stadium flyover
stories.summary: Footage of the flyover quickly began circulating on social media, prompting mixed reactions as some expressed concerns over safety.

stories.title: 'I haven't lost my hope' - the search for missing loved ones
stories.summary: Relatives of those still missing in the fatal floods in Nepal hold onto hope that their loved ones have survived.

stories.title: Across Latin America, 'aura battles' burst onto the scene
stories.summary: Young people across Latin America are taking part in the contests where participants compete to prove who has the most charisma.

stories.title: Watch: Moment Duane 'Keffe D' Davis is found guilty of Tupac Shakur's murder
stories.summary: The rapper's killing became one of popular culture's great mysteries, with countless theories but no arrests until 2023.

stories.title: Rybakina tops WTA live rankings as US Open gets underway
stories.summary: Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina has moved to the top of the WTA live rankings as the 2026 US Open begins, putting her in contention to become the world's official No. 1 for the first time.

stories.title: Jury convicts Duane 'Keffe D' Davis of first degree murder in 1996 killing of hip-hop icon Tupac Shakur
stories.summary: The verdict lays to rest decades of speculation and conspiracy from avid hip-hop fans around the world in the high-profile killing that went unresolved for close to 30 years. Davis is expected to appeal the conviction.

stories.title: 'I've never been to Afghanistan': Six million deportees forced to start over under the Taliban
stories.summary: As of August, the number forced to return this year from Pakistan and Iran had reached another million.

stories.title: Two dead and one still unaccounted for in Grand Canyon flash floods, officials say
stories.summary: Rescue efforts were hampered on Monday by more heavy rains that swept through the region, a natural part of the seasonal monsoon that frequently causes flash floods.

stories.title: US teen charged with aiding San Diego mosque shooters share livestream and manifesto
stories.summary: Sarah Santiago, 17, will be charged as an adult, according to a press release issued by prosecutor James O'Neill's office.

stories.title: Death toll passes 1,000 from catastrophic flooding in Nepal and China, officials say
stories.summary: The 26 August disaster began with a chain of events high in the Himalayas. A glacial collapse sent large amounts of rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods downstream.

stories.summary: Trump met Kim three times during his first term, once declaring they were "in love," in high-profile summits aimed at securing a denuclearisation deal, but no tangible progress was made.
